items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Harry Allen would pick them up... [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, were they.

ctx.x: But I mean it was unmistak— he might not look like what you remember Cannonball to look like, but when that alto started it was definitely Cannonball man. Oh my God. And he was such a great guy. I mean just like I just played this set with Clark Terry. And it was so encouraging — I’d play a lick and Clark would be like, “Yeah, man.” I mean this is actually, this is not just somebody sitting in the front row there, this is Clark Terry, egging you on and just kind of supporting you and stuff. And I leaned over to…

You know when — I don’t know how you put it into words, but you hear those, like he was playing some riffs, it was the first set before he played, and Harry Allen would pick them up. But these riffs he came up with were so uniquely him.
